well: ODP Hole 151-909C - CENTRAL FRAM STRAIT, North Greenland Sea (78.5849 N, 3.0704 E; seafloor -2,529 m), the ARCTIC GATEWAY - the only deep-water connection between the Arctic and world oceans; ODP Leg 151 (1993), the early-Miocene organic-rich interval 879.34-1056.91 mbsf (~12.1-17.4 Ma per the in-table age model)
operator_on_log: Knies & Mann (NGU/SINTEF) - Rock-Eval per Behar et al. 2001 (cited with DOI in the header) + MICROSCOPE maceral counts (vitrinite+huminite / liptodetrinite / marine alginite), terrestrial-vs-marine TOC partition, accumulation rates and paleoproductivity; drilling by JOIDES Resolution
source_database: PANGAEA, dataset doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.746742 ('Organic carbon chemistry of ODP Hole 151-909C (Table 1)'); supplement to Knies & Mann 2002, Marine and Petroleum Geology 19, 811-828 (doi:10.1016/S0264-8172(02)00090-9); full abstract preserved in the header including the study's R0 ~0.5 pct vitrinite-reflectance maturity context
license: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported (CC-BY-3.0), declared IN the file's own header and license-checked BEFORE cataloguing. Attribution: Knies/Mann / PANGAEA / ODP
fetch_method: read-only HTTPS fetch of the PANGAEA textfile export - COMPLETE dataset (156 data points per the header's own Size declaration, re-counted EXACT at gate time: 12 rows x 13 counted columns with BOTH geocodes - depth AND age - excluded, label counted) in one fetch
coverage: COMPLETE DATASET: 12 samples through the Miocene source-rock interval - TOC 0.79-2.87 pct partitioned into terrestrial (0.76-2.43) and marine (0.02-0.44) fractions, HI 33.3-176.7, sedimentation rate 3.34 cm/ka, dry-bulk density, terrestrial/marine accumulation rates, paleoproductivity, and three-maceral petrography (vitrinite+huminite 77.85-91.38 pct)
curves: SR 3.34 cm/ka + DBD + accumulation rates + paleoproductivity
source_anomaly_disclosure: THREE quirks preserved verbatim, each proven by arithmetic: (1) the three-maceral sum closes at 100.00 +/- 0.01 on ELEVEN of twelve rows but row 102R-2,105-10 sums to 103.18 - a 3.18-point slip in one archived maceral cell, the exception that proves the closure; (2) a UNITS MISLABEL provable by magnitude: the accumulation-rate columns are labeled g/m**2/ka but their values reproduce C x SR x DBD only in g/cm**2/ka (within 18 pct, vs a factor-10,000 miss under the printed unit); (3) EIGHT of twelve sample labels carry a truncated cm-interval (e.g. '124-12' for 124-126, an impossible end<start interval) - a systematic field-width clip in the archive; noted also: ages are Miocene millions expressed in ka (17370 ka = 17.37 Ma), consistent and correct
purpose: forty-ninth catalogue entry - the FRAM STRAIT joins as region THIRTY-SIX (the Arctic gateway: the one deep doorway between the Arctic and the world ocean, 79 N) and ORGANIC PETROGRAPHY is kind THIRTY-EIGHT - microscope-counted maceral fractions, the visual complement to the catalogue's Rock-Eval screen: not what the kerogen yields but WHAT IT IS; the source-rock verdict is re-derived on every gate run: the TOC partition closes EXACTLY on all 12 rows (terrestrial + marine = total to the last 0.01), terrestrial carbon is >= 81 pct of TOC everywhere with vitrinite+huminite >= 77.85 pct of the macerals (type III land plants rafted to 79 N by Miocene rivers), HI never reaches 200, and the archived 3.34 cm/ka sedimentation rate re-derives from the table's own dual geocodes (depth span / age span = 3.338) - a fair-to-good but immature source rock, exactly as the abstract's R0 ~0.5 pct concludes
verified: 12 rows / 156 counted cells against the header's own Size declaration (EXACT with both geocodes excluded); TOC = ter + mar identity 12/12 EXACT (worst 0.000); maceral closure 11/12 within 0.01 with the single 103.18 slip pinned; accumulation-rate magnitude check pins the g/cm2/ka reading (worst 18 pct vs 10^4 under the label); depth-span/age-span = 3.338 vs archived 3.34; 8 truncated labels pinned; terrestrial fraction >= 0.809 and HI <= 176.7 and TOC max 2.87 pinned; gate-pinned; source URL serves the identical dataset
